pages.text: "I don't like here! I want the old shore!" Kiki hid behind Mom's legs. Heavy overnight rain had spread the waterhole into the reeds. Thicker reeds, strange smells, unfamiliar birds—everything had changed.
Mom lowered her head. "Rain makes the waterhole grow. This is our shore now." Kiki hugged her leg. "Everything's new... I want yesterday's shore."
Kiki crouched behind a rock and peeked out. A strange large bird flapped, and the reeds swished. "It's all unfamiliar... I'm alone."
Mom lay gently beside the rock. "A new shore feels strange to everyone. Watch me." She touched her muzzle to the water. "Hello, water!" It rippled like an answer. Kiki's head rose a little.
Moya returned from a run around the waterhole. "Kiki! This rock is so high—perfect for a lookout!" Moya tapped it cheerfully. Kiki's heart softened.
Mom whispered, "One hello can make a strange place familiar. Shall we say 'Hello, new waterhole'?" Kiki climbed gently onto the rock. Moya nodded below.
Kiki stood tall and opened their chest. "Hello, new waterhole! Hello, rock! Hello, reeds!" The reeds swished and the big bird called back. The unfamiliar shore felt familiar now.
From the rock, Kiki surveyed the waterhole, reeds, and red dirt path. "What a great lookout spot!" Kiki gave their first big laugh. Moya bounced below.
Now Kiki knew the steps. "One, stay by Mom and look when it's unfamiliar! Two, say hello! Three, look around from somewhere high!" At sunset, a little bird landed. Kiki greeted it first.
Mom cuddled Kiki with her muzzle. "You did so well, even when it felt strange!" One hello could make a new place familiar. Hello, new waterhole!
